properties.name: Split-capstone on 0.90.0 (FICTIONAL): one organisation's released product rolls up into another's design by mirror_surface, under need-to-know. But when the product is superseded, the refreshed mirror DELETES the withdrawn judgments and the reasoning edges into them, so nothing reports that any decision lost its reason. The one-design capstone (10-19) did report it.
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-10-22. Designs:
- Intel e195be3c56cb2d89;
- Acquisition b5caab36bcd16c80.
Both are FICTIONAL, both are hub members, on reflow2 0.90.0.
- Two designer agents, one per organisation, plus the observer as COURIER, who carried only the released product's export_surface `document`.
- Observer notes: scratchpad split-capstone-trial/OBSERVER.md, plus courier/.
- No cause is asserted here; these are observations, to root-cause before fixing.

ROUND 1 WORKED:
- Intel kept its reasoning in its own design: graded reports, assessment, contested hypotheses.
- It released KESTREL-ASSESS v1 as a published Interface, plus an Artifact holding the product text, plus 4 published judgments with confidence.
- The surface exposed 8 nodes and withheld 30 nodes and 87 edges.
- Acquisition mirrored it (pinned by hash) and built decisions (a) X band, (b) design for agility, (c) 220 km on 75 dBW, each concluded by a step resting on the mirrored judgments.
- FINDINGS:
  - mirrored judgments read truth "unknown" (requirement status), so CONFIDENCE plays no part, and nothing can read broken;
  - mirrored nodes are credited to the importer (AUTHORED_BY who:ajs);
  - key assumptions travel only as prose;
  - the only watch (design_address) reads the whole foreign design, so need-to-know blocks it;
  - a near-leak: export_surface without `member` ran on the hub's own design.

ROUND 2, THE FINDING: Intel recorded U1 (A1) and released v2 (Ku band; v1's waveform and ERP withdrawn), superseding v1 by OBSOLETES. The courier carried it (text hash verified). On acquisition's re-mirror:
1. The first call was REFUSED: "no longer publishes 4 boundary(ies) that YOUR design still points at", counting DEPENDS_ON and ASKS_ABOUT edges only. It did NOT count the 7 PREMISE_OF edges that decisions (a), (b) and (c) rest on.
2. After those 6 edges were removed, the refresh returned refreshed: true and withdrawn: [v1 KJ1–KJ4]. It DELETED those nodes ("no node … under ANY declared type"), with no snapshot and no ChangeEvent, and silently dropped every local edge touching mirrored nodes: the PREMISE_OF reasoning edges, CONSUMES, CALIBRATED_AGAINST, DOCUMENTS and re-pointed ASKS_ABOUT.
3. Afterwards, reasoning_report on (a), (b) and (c) read exactly as before, minus the vanished premises: (a) now "rests on" the mission need alone. propagate_from on the withdrawn judgments returned unknown_seeds and 0 impacted. loop_status showed reasons_lost 0 and stale_checks 0.
4. `mirrors` moved to the v2 hash and kept no history. The declared pin still named v1, and nothing compared the two.

So the split loses exactly the signal the one-design capstone gave: "this decision's reason is gone". The designer found every lost reason only by reading v2.

The re-decided design: (d) a new Ku-band coverage decision; (a) kept, re-grounded on v2 KJ2; (b) and (c) superseded by (b2) and (c2). All are proposed. Old (b) and (c) "still count" until the owner accepts their successors.

WHAT THIS MEANS for Anthony's accepted option (b), separate reasoning designs with roll-ups: the roll-up works for a first release, but is NOT YET SAFE across a superseding release. A superseded judgment must remain (superseded, never deleted), keep the edges that rest on it, and make those decisions read as having lost their reason.
